Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — high-context multi-model service

Hi Jonas / Laura,

We're sizing a dedicated inference pool for ZenCli's new product line. High level: we run two primary model families in production — a 70B chat model for interactive agents (typical context 8k, spike to 32k for long threads) and a separate 13B reranker for batch scoring. Both use KV caching aggressively on the chat side.

We need a ballpark for:
- GPU count and memory profile to guarantee 99th % latency SLOs for interactive flows
- Headroom assumptions for KV cache (multiple simultaneous sessions with warm cache)
- Impact of going from FP16 -> INT8 or 4-bit on capacity (memory and throughput)

I'm attaching a small traffic sample and a CSV of session lengths. Can you share a quick sizing estimate and any opt-in quantization risks we should be aware of (quality regressions, fallback strategies)?

Would prefer this week if possible — we have procurement timelines on Oct 4.

Thanks,
Katherine
Katherine Lee
Head of Platform, ZenCli

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — high-context multi-model service

Jonas / Laura / Katherine — dug into the sample and ran quick roughs. Notes and conservative recommendations below. I'm attaching a short spreadsheet with the per-request KV memory simulation (zencli-kv-sensitivity.xlsx) and a draft MAP (minimal accepted plan) for the pool.

Key assumptions I used (from your sample and industry defaults):
- Chat model: 70B architecture, baseline FP16 memory footprint ~40GB for weights in GPU memory (model sharded across 2-way tensors on our serving runtime). KV cache per token: ~2.4 KB (includes keys+values and metadata) when fully warmed. Typical interactive request generates 64 tokens; long-thread spike generates 4000 tokens appended to KV.
- Reranker: 13B, FP16 ~10GB weight footprint, batch-oriented, average batch size 128 per GPU.
- Concurrency: 250 concurrent interactive sessions with average of 1.6 requests/sec/session; 30% of sessions have long-thread spikes once per hour.

Sizing table (conservative headroom + 30% buffer for autoscaling and tail):
- Chat (70B): FP16 -> target per-GPU usable memory 80GB (we provision on 80GB A100 equivalent). To support 250 concurrent sessions with KV cache:
  - KV memory: 250 sessions * avg 64 tokens/session * 2.4KB/token = ~38.4GB (steady state).
  - Spike headroom (30% sessions hitting 4k tokens): additional ~72GB if all occur simultaneously (unlikely) — we size for a 25% simultaneous spike probability -> 18GB additional.
  - Total working set (weights + KV warm): 40GB + 38.4GB + 18GB = ~96.4GB -> mapped across 2 GPUs (sharding) -> ~48.2GB per GPU.
  - Recommendation: 2x80GB GPUs per shard pair (4 GPUs total) to maintain headroom and allow eviction/continuous batching. Operationally we'd recommend starting with 4x80GB GPUs dedicated (can scale to 6 if early metrics show higher tail usage).

- Reranker (13B): FP16 weights ~10GB + ephemeral activation ~6GB per batch -> one 80GB GPU can host multiple batches. Conservative estimate: 2x80GB GPUs to handle peak batch scoring with headroom.

Quantization impact (memory and throughput):
- INT8: weight memory drops ~50-60% (70B weight from 40GB -> ~16-20GB), KV cache unchanged (KV is activation-like, remains similar unless we quantize cache representation, which we're not recommending). Throughput improves ~1.6-2x but risk: some instruction-level quality regressions on edge cases (rare hallucination shifts).
- 4-bit (QLoRA-type mixed): weights down to ~11GB; throughput ~2.2-2.8x vs FP16 in optimized kernels; higher risk on instruction-following and diversity of prompts. More careful eval required per task set.

Operational recommendation:
1) Start with FP16 baseline sizing above and run a controlled INT8 benchmark on representative prompt set. If quality delta is <1–2% on your evals, move critical read paths to INT8 and reserve FP16 fallback for flagged prompts.
2) For KV cache: add a lightweight eviction policy (LRU by session age) and a soft limit per session (e.g., 6k tokens) to limit unbounded growth; surface cache pressure metrics to SLO dashboards.
3) Reserve 25–30% thermal headroom per GPU for batching spikes and model updates.

Suggested immediate technical deliverables (this week):
- Short benchmark run: INT8 vs FP16 on 1000 representative requests (we can run in our dedicated sandbox) -> expected runtime 2–4 hours. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/zencli/benchmarks/mini-int8-run-20260925
- Draft SOW/Capacity MAP attached (draft-MAP.pdf) with proposed 4x80GB + 2x80GB for reranker start.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regressions on low-frequency tokens/prompt patterns: mitigate with fallback to FP16 and automatic A/B monitoring.
- KV cache blowouts from bad clients: enforce per-session caps and alerting.

Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Capacity Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: zencli-kv-sensitivity.xlsx (xlsx), draft-MAP.pdf (pdf)

- "Start with 4x80GB GPUs for chat (70B) + 2x80GB for reranker (13B); enable INT8 pilot on 30% of traffic with automatic FP16 fallback" — is that accurate?
